summary: A dense Vital Lacerda worker-placement engine-builder where you develop invention cards through stages (idea to invention to global spread), pulling levers across several interlocking boards to generate Intellectual Property Points. Turns are quiet and heads-down as each player optimizes their own engine, with occasional friction over shared worker-placement spots and card availability.
praised: Tight, elegant interlocking systems typical of Lacerda's design
Strong sense of building an engine and watching it snowball
High replayability from variable inventions and multiple viable paths to points
Satisfying puzzle of sequencing actions efficiently
criticised: Steep rules overhead and long teach/setup time
Heavy iconography that takes several plays to internalize
Analysis paralysis due to the number of simultaneous considerations
Low direct interaction can make multiplayer feel like parallel solitaire
High cost of entry (price, table space) for a niche heavy-gamer audience

interaction.kind: mostly parallel engine-building with light blocking over shared worker spots and card draft

scoring.why: IPP accumulates from multiple systems (developing and spreading inventions, technology/economy/culture tracks, and bonus objectives), so the winner is whoever best diversifies and chains these scoring avenues
